relevance_reason: Phase 2-3 trial of emapalumab in children with primary HLH (genetic subtypes not given in the abstract). It is relevant to clinical management of familial HLH, including FHL4, but does not report FHL4-specific patients or variants.

findings.statement: Locatelli et al. (2020) reported an open-label, single-group, phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone to patients aged 18 years or younger with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Of 34 treated patients (27 previously treated and 7 previously untreated), 63% of previously treated patients and 65% of all patients who received emapalumab had a response, which was significantly higher than the prespecified null hypothesis of 40%. Seventy percent of previously treated patients went on to transplantation. Emapalumab was not associated with organ toxicity, but severe infections developed in 10 patients, and treatment was stopped in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.
quotes: At the cutoff date of July 20, 2017, a total of 34 patients (27 previously treated patients and 7 previously untreated patients) had received emapalumab; 26 patients completed the study.

A total of 63% of the previously treated patients and 65% of the patients who received an emapalumab infusion had a response; these percentages were significantly higher than the prespecified null hypothesis of 40% (P = 0.02 and P = 0.005, respectively).

Emapalumab was not associated with any organ toxicity. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during emapalumab treatment. Emapalumab was discontinued in 1 patient because of disseminated histoplasmosis.

relevance_reason: Reports a novel homozygous STX11 missense mutation (L58P) in three unrelated Pakistani FHL4 patients with clinical, functional and biochemical characterization.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2014) described 3 children (2 males, 1 female) from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families who presented with HLH at ages 2 months, 5 years, and 48 months. Patients A and B had fever, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia, without hemophagocytosis or neurologic manifestations. They were treated with dexamethasone, cyclosporine A, and etoposide and were in remission at 2 months, but both died; patient A had undergone HSCT at 15 months. Patient C was lost to follow-up.
quotes: Here, we describe two infants and one 5-year-old child born to unrelated Pakistani families that presented with HLH (Table 1).
Age at diagnosis-HLH | 2 months | 5 years | 48 months
Outcome | Deceased | Deceased | nd

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2014) found that all 3 patients had defective NK cell lysis of K562 target cells and defective NK cell degranulation, which were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation; expression of perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal, suggesting intact granule integrity.
quotes: All patients displayed defective lysis of K562 target cells and degranulation by NK cells in response to K562 target cells or engagement of the Fc receptor CD16 (Figures 1A,B).
Notably, cytotoxicity and degranulation were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation (Figures 1C,D).
expression of cytotoxic granule constituents’ perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a was normal in patient NK cells, suggesting that granule integrity was not impaired

findings.statement: In 3 patients from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families with FHL4, Müller et al. (2014) identified a novel homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in an alpha-helix of the predicted Habc domain, by sequencing of UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2. Parents were heterozygous and had no history of inflammatory disease.
quotes: Sequencing of the coding regions and splice-sites of UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2 revealed that all three patients were homozygous for a novel STX11 mutation, c.173T > C (p.L58P) (Table 1).
The parents were heterozygous for this STX11 mutation, but did not have any recorded history of inflammatory disease.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2014) noted that patient A, who also carried a heterozygous UNC13D P271S variant and a homozygous UNC13D R928C variant, presented earlier and showed less restoration of NK cell degranulation after IL-2 stimulation; they suggested the UNC13D variants might contribute to disease severity.
quotes: patient A was heterozygous for a rare UNC13D c.811C > T (p.P271S; frequency 0.001 in a Caucasian population of 4294 individuals) variant inherited from the father and homozygous for an uncommon UNC13D c.2782C > T (p.R928C, frequency 0.01
it is possible that the UNC13D variants contribute to the severity of disease presentation in patient A.

findings.statement: Müller et al. (2014) found greatly reduced syntaxin-11 expression in PBMCs and LAK cells from patient C, with normal Munc18-2 levels. In transfected HEK293T cells, L58P and an N-peptide R4A mutant were expressed at wildtype levels but failed to bind Munc18-2, whereas the FHL4-associated Q268X mutant bound normally. The authors concluded that both the N-terminus and Habc domain of syntaxin-11 are required for Munc18-2 binding and suggested that loss of this interaction destabilizes syntaxin-11 in patient cells.
quotes: LAK cells from the patient also displayed a selective loss of Stx11 expression, whereas Munc18-2 expression was similar to that of control LAK cells (Figure 3B).
Notably, in pull-down experiments using beads loaded with FLAG-tagged Stx11 wild-type and Stx11 mutants neither FLAG-tagged Stx11 R4A nor L58P mutants bound HA-tagged Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).
In contrast, the C-terminal Stx11 Q268X mutation previously associated with FHL4, did not display impaired binding of Munc18-2 (Figure 4E).

relevance_reason: Reports STX11 mutations in FHL families (FHL4) with clinical characterization including remissions, psychomotor retardation and MDS/AML.

findings.statement: Rudd et al. (2006) performed direct sequencing of STX11 in 28 FHL families without PRF1 mutations and identified 2 different previously reported STX11 mutations, a nonsense mutation and a deletion, in 6 of 34 children from 4 of the 28 unrelated families. STX11 mutations accounted for 14% of the PRF1-negative FHL families in the cohort.
quotes: Mutational analysis of STX11 by direct sequencing was done in 28 FHL families that did not harbour perforin mutations

Two different STX11 mutations were identified, one nonsense mutation and one deletion, affecting six of 34 children in four of 28 unrelated PRF1 negative families. Both mutations have been reported before.
STX11 gene mutations were found in 14% of the PRF1 negative FHL families included in the present cohort.

findings.statement: Rudd et al. (2006) found that 3 of 6 patients with STX11 mutations experienced long periods (1 year or more) of remission without specific treatment, which is very uncommon in FHL. Despite this milder phenotype, some children with STX11 mutations developed severe psychomotor retardation.
quotes: Three patients experienced long periods (> or = 1 year) in remission without specific treatment, which is very uncommon in this disease.
Despite the milder phenotype, some children with STX11 mutations developed severe psychomotor retardation.

phenotypes.text: prolonged disease-free remission without specific treatment

findings.statement: Rudd et al. (2006) reported that 2 of 6 patients with STX11 mutations developed myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myelogenous leukemia, and suggested that STX11 mutations may be associated with secondary hematopoietic malignancies.
quotes: Two of the six patients harbouring STX11 gene defects developed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or acute myelogenous leukaemia (AML).
These results suggest that STX11 gene mutations may be associated with secondary malignancies (MDS/AML)

findings.statement: Rudd et al. (2006) concluded that there is segregation of specific clinical features, including disease-free remissions and haematopoietic malignancies, in FHL patients according to underlying genotype, with STX11 mutation carriers showing a milder phenotype.
quotes: there is segregation of specific clinical features in FHL patients with an underlying genotype.

relevance_reason: This is a mutation screen of 63 unrelated patients with FHL. It found STX11 (FHL4) mutations in 6 Turkish patients and none in German patients or patients of other origins, which adds evidence on the frequency and population distribution of FHL4.

findings.statement: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) screened 63 unrelated patients with FHL from Turkey (32), Germany (23) and other origins (8) for mutations in STX11, PRF1 and UNC13D. They found mutations in 38 patients: 20 in PRF1, 12 in UNC13D and 6 in STX11. All 6 patients with STX11 mutations were from Turkey; none of the German patients or patients of other origins had STX11 mutations.
quotes: We analyzed a large group of 63 unrelated patients with FHL of different geographic origins (Turkey:32; Germany:23; others:8) for mutations in STX11, PRF1, and UNC13D. We identified mutations in 38 samples (20 in PRF1, 12 in UNC13D, and six in STX11).
Of 32 patients from Turkey, 14 had mutations in PRF1, six had mutations in UNC13D, and six had mutations in STX11.
In contrast, three of 23 and four of 23 patients from Germany, and three of eight and two of eight from other origins showed mutations in PRF1 and UNC13D, respectively, but none in STX11.

findings.statement: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) reported that FHL2, FHL3 and FHL4 together accounted for 80% of HLH cases of Turkish origin and 30% of German cases. STX11 mutations (FHL4) were found only in Turkish patients (6 of 32).
quotes: Thus, FHL-2, FHL-3, and FHL-4 account for 80% of the HLH cases of Turkish origin, and for 30% of German patients.

findings.statement: Zur Stadt et al. (2006) concluded that FHL shows extensive genetic and allelic heterogeneity. Mutations were found in PRF1, UNC13D and STX11, and RAB27A mutations were found in 3 patients with FHL-related Griscelli syndrome type 2.
quotes: Our findings demonstrate extensive genetic and allelic heterogeneity in FHL and delineate an approach for functionally characterizing missense mutations in RAB27A and UNC13D.
Furthermore, we identified mutations in RAB27A in three patients with FHL-related Griscelli syndrome type 2.

relevance_reason: This paper reports the mapping of FHL4 to 6q24 and identifies homozygous STX11 mutations in consanguineous Kurdish and Turkish families.

findings.statement: zur Stadt et al. (2005) performed genome-wide homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with 5 children affected with FHL. They found linkage to a 10-cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960, which defined a new FHL locus.
quotes: We performed genome-wide homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with five children affected with FHL.
Linkage to a 10 cM region on chromosome 6q24 between D6S1569 and D6S960 defined a novel FHL locus.

findings.statement: In the consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL linked to 6q24, zur Stadt et al. (2005) screened positional candidate genes and identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent from the mononuclear cell fraction of patients who were homozygous for the deletion. The same homozygous 5-bp deletion was also found in 2 additional consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds.
quotes: By screening positional candidate genes, we identified a homozygous deletion of 5 bp in the syntaxin 11 gene (STX11) in this family.
We could demonstrate that syntaxin 11 protein was absent in the mononuclear cell fraction of patients with the homozygous 5 bp deletion.
including two families with the 5 bp deletion

findings.statement: zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 19.2-kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2) in 1 consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindred.
quotes: one family with a large 19.2 kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2)

variants.as_reported: 19.2 kb genomic deletion spanning the entire coding region of STX11 (exon 2)

findings.statement: In 2 consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in STX11 that leads to a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein.
quotes: two families with a nonsense mutation that leads to a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein

variants.as_reported: nonsense mutation that leads to a premature stop codon in the C-terminal end of the protein

findings.statement: Because both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, zur Stadt et al. (2005) concluded that defects in the endocytotic or exocytotic pathway, in addition to perforin mutations, may be a common mechanism in FHL.
quotes: As both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, we conclude that, besides mutations in perforin 1, defects in the endocytotic or the exocytotic pathway may be a common mechanism in FHL.

findings.statement: zur Stadt et al. (2005) noted that FHL is genetically heterogeneous: mutations in PRF1 and UNC13D underlie FHL2 and FHL3, respectively, and the 6q24 locus with STX11 mutations defined a new FHL locus.
quotes: It has been shown previously that mutations in the perforin 1 gene (PRF1) and in UNC13D are associated with FHL2 and FHL3, respectively, indicating genetic heterogeneity.
